newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Israeli president's son detained in France.
newsitem.headline: Former Israeli president's son detained in France.

text.p: Joel Herzog, son of former Israeli president Haim Herzog, was taken into custody after being placed under investigation for suspected complicity in a French corruption scandal on Monday, justice sources said.

Herzog, 47, was suspected of complicity in the payment of a 1.45 million franc ($290,000) bribe to Michel Mouillot, mayor of the French Riviera city of Cannes who is himself in jail awaiting trial, the sources said.
Herzog, who is being held in Grasse prison, resides in Switzerland and holds dual Israeli and British nationality.
He was placed under investigation in his capacity as an associate of international businessman Nissim Gaon whose empire includes the Noga-Hilton hotel in Cannes.
Herzog is married to Gaon's daughter and is an administrator in the Noga group.
The case involves a requested municipal permit to place an additional 100 slot machines in the Grand Riviera Casino situated inside the Noga-Hilton, the sources said.
The magistrate investigating the case asked both Herzog and Gaon to appear in his chambers while warning them they might be placed in custody.

Herzog came alone while lawyers for his 74-year-old father-in-law presented the magistrate with a written statement alleging the money was paid to Mouillot after pressure and threats from the politician, justice sources said.
Another senior Noga group official, Briton Martin Conway, was placed in custody on November 22 after also being placed under investigation in the same case.
Judicial sources said Conway told the magistrate that the Noga group paid the 1.45 million francs in four instalments ahead of a Cannes municipal council vote on the slot machine installation.

Lawyers Ricard Banon and Daniel Diedler who accompanied Herzog told reporters their client presented himself spontaneously and was placed under custody because magistrates felt that was the only way they could establish the facts clearly.
"This will be done without inhibition (by Herzog)," Banon said.

Mouillot has been jailed since July, together with his son and several aides, on charges of seeking bribes from a British gambling group in exchange for permits to set up or expand casinos in the glitzy Riviera resort.
Mouillot's lawyers have alleged he was the victim of political infighting between members of the ruling centre-right coalition.
Mouillot is a member of the coalition's junior partner, the centre-right Union for French Democracy.
